rows.title: Phase-transition conjecture for unimodality of Fuss–Catalan distributions
rows.record_statement:
Let $p>1$ and let $\mu(p,r)$ denote the Fuss–Catalan distribution with parameters $p$ and $r$. **Phase-transition conjecture.** For every $p>1$ there exists $r_{0}(p)$ satisfying

$$
p-1<r_{0}(p)<p,
$$

such that $\mu(p,r)$ is unimodal if and only if either $r=p$ or $0<r\leqslant r_{0}(p)$. This conjecture is suggested by the results in the preceding sections and by numerical experiments; the general phase transition remains open.
rows.source: Wojciech Młotkowski, Noriyoshi Sakuma and Yuki Ueda, “Free self-decomposability and unimodality of the Fuss-Catalan distributions”, arXiv:1908.07887 (2019).
rows.what_was_proved: For every p > 1 there is r0 with p - 1 < r0 < p such that, for 0 < r <= p, the Fuss-Catalan distribution mu(p, r) is unimodal if and only if r = p or r <= r0. Lean proves this for the measure with the explicit density of the source's Proposition 1.1, formula (2) (due to Forrester and Liu), with unimodality in the source's sense (an atom plus a density nondecreasing before and nonincreasing after the mode). That this measure is the moment-defined distribution mu(p, r), total mass one included, is the source's published Proposition 1.1, cited and not checked in Lean. The proof shows that the logarithmic derivative of the density is strictly decreasing in r, so the unimodal parameters form an interval, and locates its endpoint strictly between p - 1 and p.

rows.title: Congruence conjecture for signed power sums of Franel numbers
rows.record_statement:
For nonnegative integers $n$ and $r$, define

$$
f_{n}^{(r)}=\sum_{k=0}^n{n\choose k}^r.
$$

In particular, $f_n^{(3)}=f_n$ are the Franel numbers. **The signed Franel congruence conjecture.** Let $n\geq 1$ and $r\geq 0$ be two integers. Then

$$
\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(-1)^{rk}(3k+2)f_{k}^{(r)}\equiv 0\pmod {2n}.
$$

This conjecture unifies the preceding congruences and Sun's fourth-power case; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
rows.source: Victor J. W. Guo, “Proof of two conjectures of Z.-W. Sun on congruences for Franel numbers”, arXiv:1201.0617 (2012).
rows.what_was_proved: For all integers n >= 1 and r >= 0, 2n divides the sum over k from 0 to n - 1 of (-1)^(rk) (3k + 2) f_k^(r), where f_k^(r) is the sum of the r-th powers of the binomial coefficients C(k, j). This is Conjecture 4.1 of Guo, who proved the cases r <= 3. The proof deforms the sum to a polynomial in q with Gaussian binomials, putting the weight q^(n-1-k)[k+j+1] on half of the sum, shows by the q-Lucas theorem and a block factorization with its phase signs that the deformation vanishes at every n-th root of unity other than 1, divides by the monic polynomial [n] over the integers, and sets q = 1; the factor 2 comes from the symmetry of the half-sum. Lean states the congruence in the integers exactly as printed, for every n >= 1 and every natural r.

rows.title: Injectivity conjecture for evaluation maps of linearized polynomials
rows.record_statement:
Let $L=L(x)$ be a $q$-polynomial in $F[x]$ of $q$-degree $n$, where $F$ is a field of characteristic $p$ that contains $\operatorname{\mathbb{F}}_q$. Assume that $L$ is not a $q^s$-polynomial for $s>1$, and that $L(x)/x$ is irreducible over $F$.

**Injectivity conjecture.** If $1\le r\le q-1$, then the evaluation map $\epsilon_r$ is injective.

This conjecture predicts injectivity in the range $1\le r\le q-1$ under irreducibility and a non-$q^s$-polynomial hypothesis. The surrounding results establish related injectivity statements for evaluation maps, but the supplied text does not state whether this conjecture has been resolved.
rows.source: Rod Gow and Gary McGuire, “Linearized Polynomials, Galois Groups and Symmetric Power Modules”, arXiv:2206.01551 (2022).
rows.what_was_proved: Conjecture 1 of Gow and McGuire is false. Over F = F_3(t) the 3-polynomial L = X^81 + (t + t^2) X^27 - (t + t^2) X^9 + (t + t^2) X^3 - t (t^2 + t + 1) X has 3-degree 4, L/X is irreducible over F, L is not a 3^s-polynomial for any s > 1, and r = 2 <= q - 1, yet the evaluation map epsilon_2 on quadratic forms in a basis of the root space is not injective: an explicit seven-term quadratic form vanishes on the roots (the image has dimension 8 in a space of dimension 10). The roots are the image of u F_81, with u^80 = t, under the additive twist x -> x + x^3 of the Kummer polynomial X^81 - tX; the twist keeps irreducibility, because the automorphisms u -> cu act transitively on the nonzero roots, and it forces the kernel. Lean states the conjecture for q = p = 3 with every hypothesis of the source and proves its negation with this witness, including irreducibility and the splitting field.

rows.title: Minimality conjecture for initial threshold graphs generated by RFI
rows.record_statement: Let $N>0$ and $r\geq 2$ be fixed, and let $I=(0,N]$. Let $T_G(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$ be the initial threshold graph obtained from RFI$(N,r)$. **Minimality conjecture.** The graph $G$ is minimal: if $\widetilde{G}\preceq G$ is also $I$-eigenvalue free, then $\widetilde{G}=G$. This conjecture asserts that no smaller threshold graph is $(0,N]$-eigenvalue free. The authors report exhaustive computational searches for several positive values of $N$ that found no smaller example, but the general claim remains open.
rows.source: Luiz Emilio Allem, Elismar R. Oliveira and Fernando Tura, “On I-eigenvalue free threshold graphs”, arXiv:2110.12107 (2021).
rows.what_was_proved: For every real N > 0 and every depth r >= 2, the threshold graph that the source's algorithm produces with the smallest choice at every step is minimal: any threshold graph of the same depth whose block sizes are coordinatewise at most those of the initial graph and which has no adjacency eigenvalue in (0, N] is the initial graph itself. The source's authors conjectured this after exhaustive searches of millions of graphs. The proof reduces freeness of the interval to positive definiteness of a k x k matrix (k = ceil(r/2)) by the block structure and a Schur complement on the independent blocks, and shows that every single decrement of a block fails: for a clique block the pivot at the greedy threshold becomes nonpositive, and for an independent block a floor inequality makes the pivot of the pair formed with the preceding clique block nonpositive. Lean defines the graph on a sigma type, the algorithm with real floors, and the eigenvalue condition through adjacency eigenvectors, and includes a non-vacuity lemma.

rows.title: Carnevale–Voll's factorisation conjecture for multiset Euler–Mahonian polynomials
rows.record_statement:
Let $\eta$ be a composition, and let $S_{\eta}$ denote the associated multiset permutations. For a polynomial $f\in\mathbb{Z}[x,y]$, call it **unitary** if there are $F\in\mathbb{Z}[Y]$ and $a,b\in\mathbb{N}_0$ such that $f(x,y)=F(x^ay^b)$ and every complex root of $F$ has absolute value $1$.

**Carnevale–Voll's factorisation conjecture.** The polynomial giving the joint distribution of $(\operatorname{den},\operatorname{exc})$ over $S_{\eta}$ has a unitary factor if and only if $\eta=(m^r)$ is a rectangle with $r$ even and $m$ odd. In that case,

$$
\sum_{w\in S_{\eta}}x^{\operatorname{den}(w)}y^{\operatorname{exc}(w)}=\left(1+x^{\frac{rm}{2}}y\right)f^{\eta}_0(x,y),
$$

where $f^{\eta}_0(x,y)$ has no unitary factor.

This is a reformulation of the factorisation conjecture for joint $(\operatorname{des},\operatorname{maj})$ distributions over multiset permutations. The stated factorisation singles out the unitary factor $1+x^{rm/2}y$ in exactly the even-by-odd rectangular cases; its resolution is not given in the supplied text.
rows.source: Angela Carnevale and Elena Tielker, “On Denert's statistic”, arXiv:2108.04700 (2021).
rows.what_was_proved: For every composition eta, the polynomial giving the joint distribution of Denert's statistic and excedances over the multiset permutations S_eta has a (nonconstant) unitary factor if and only if eta = (m^r) is a rectangle with r even and m odd; in that case the factor is 1 + x^{rm/2} y, it occurs once, and the cofactor has no unitary factor. This is Conjecture 23 of Carnevale and Tielker, the (den, exc) form of Conjecture B of Carnevale and Voll. Lean defines the words, excedances, Denert's statistic, the polynomial and the unitary predicate literally and proves both directions, the printed factor, multiplicity one and the statement about the cofactor, under ONE named hypothesis: the source's published generating-function formula for the polynomial (its equation (10) with Theorems 3 and 10, that is MacMahon's formula transported by Han's equidistribution), which is not formalized. The new mathematics is the exclusion of non-rectangles: a unitary factor forces poles of the generating function at roots of unity whose orders are incompatible, by a strict sine-sum inequality, unless all parts are equal.

rows.title: Odd-order graphs do not exhibit Laplacian perfect state transfer
rows.record_statement: Let $X$ be a simple connected unweighted graph on an odd number of vertices. **Odd-order Laplacian PST conjecture.** Laplacian perfect state transfer does not occur in $X$. This extends the corresponding result for unweighted graphs on $3$ or $5$ vertices and follows for weighted join graphs under the additional assumption that the characteristic polynomial of the Laplacian has integer coefficients; the general case remains open.
rows.source: Steve Kirkland and Hermie Monterde, “Quantum walks on join graphs”, arXiv:2312.06906 (2023).
rows.what_was_proved: The conjecture of Kirkland and Monterde that Laplacian perfect state transfer does not occur in a simple connected unweighted graph of odd order is false. An explicit connected graph on 35 vertices has perfect state transfer between two vertices at time pi/2: two nonadjacent twin vertices u, v are joined to every vertex of a set W of 22 vertices, each vertex of W has 8 neighbours in a set R of 11 vertices, and each vertex of R has 16 neighbours in W. The Laplacian eigenvalues on the symmetric vector e_u + e_v are 0, 20 and 28, all divisible by 4, and the eigenvalue on e_u - e_v is 22, congruent to 2 modulo 4, so exp(i pi L / 2) maps e_u to e_v. The graph is the case k = 1 of a family of orders 36k^2 - 1 (r = 12k^2 - 1, c = 8k^2), proved on paper for all k. Lean checks the 35-vertex graph: it defines the conjecture for all simple connected graphs on an odd number of vertices with Mathlib's Laplacian and the complex matrix exponential, proves connectedness and the eigenvector identities by kernel computation, and derives the negation.

rows.title: The star characterization conjecture for graphs with one large Laplacian eigenvalue
rows.record_statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with Laplacian eigenvalues $\mu_1\geq\cdots\geq\mu_n$ and average degree $\overline{d}(G)=2m/n$, where $m$ is the number of edges and $n$ the number of vertices. Define $\sigma(G)$ to be the number of Laplacian eigenvalues at least $\overline{d}(G)$. For integers $r\geq 1$ and $s\geq 0$, let $K_{1,r}+sK_1$ denote the disjoint union of the star $K_{1,r}$ and $s$ isolated vertices. **Star characterization conjecture.** $\sigma(G)=1$ if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to $K_1$, $K_2+sK_1$ for some $s\geq 0$, or $K_{1,r}+sK_1$ for some $r\geq 2$ and $0\leq s<r-1$. The conjecture seeks a complete structural characterization of graphs having exactly one Laplacian eigenvalue at least their average degree; the paper proves it for several classes, including graphs whose complements are disconnected, but the general case remains open.
rows.source: L. Emilio Allem, Antonio Cafure, Ezequiel Dratman, Luciano N. Grippo, Martín D. Safe and Vilmar Trevisan, “Partial characterization of graphs having a single large Laplacian eigenvalue”, arXiv:1710.01710 (2017).
rows.what_was_proved: A graph on n >= 1 vertices has exactly one Laplacian eigenvalue greater than or equal to its average degree (sigma(G) = 1, eigenvalues counted with multiplicity) if and only if n = 1, or G is K_{1,1} with any number s of isolated vertices, or G is a star K_{1,r} with r >= 2 together with s < r - 1 isolated vertices. No connectivity is assumed; for connected graphs this says that the stars are the only graphs with sigma = 1, the conjecture of Allem, Cafure, Dratman, Grippo, Safe and Trevisan, who proved it for forests, cographs, split graphs and other classes. The proof uses the bound mu_2 >= d_2 to reduce to connected graphs with a single vertex above the average degree, takes a Schur complement at that vertex, and closes the case by a degree-deficit count. Mathlib has no Courant-Fischer theorem, so Lean builds the link between counting eigenvalues above a threshold and subspaces on which the quadratic form is large, and proves the bound on the second largest Laplacian eigenvalue.

rows.title: Strict unimodality conjecture for Reiner–Stanton polynomials
rows.record_statement:
Let

$$
F_{n,k}(q)={n+k\brack k}-q^{n}{n+k-2\brack k-2},
$$

where $k\geq 2$ and $n$ is even. A polynomial is **strictly unimodal, except for the two terms at both ends** when its coefficients strictly increase to the middle, apart from the two end terms. **Strict unimodality conjecture.** For $n\geq 8$ and $k\geq 15$, $F_{n,k}(q)$ is strictly unimodal, except for the two terms at both ends. The conjecture is supported by numerical evidence, while the text does not report a proof or disproof.
rows.source: William Y. C. Chen and Ivy D. D. Jia, “Semi-invariants of Binary Forms Pertaining to a Unimodality Theorem of Reiner and Stanton”, arXiv:2011.01467 (2021).
rows.what_was_proved: For every even n >= 8 and every k >= 15, the polynomial F_{n,k}(q) = [n+k, k]_q - q^n [n+k-2, k-2]_q is symmetric of degree nk, has f_0 = f_1, and its coefficients increase strictly from f_1 up to the centre nk/2. This is Conjecture 3.3 of Chen and Jia in the setting of their definition (3.4), where n is even, which is also how the MathDB record states it. The proof works in the ring of semi-invariants of binary forms modulo the unique invariant Q of degree 2: that quotient is a domain, so the set of degrees in which a coefficient difference is positive is closed under addition; Sylvester's theorem identifies the differences with dimensions; uniform seeds in a few small degrees come from a quasipolynomial certificate for restricted partitions (3,632 residue cases, each a polynomial identity plus a sign check, with the coverage of all cases proved in Lean); a covering argument and a separate induction for n = 10 and 14 finish. Lean defines the Gaussian binomial as a sum over partitions in a box and proves the statement literally.

rows.title: Thue–Morse arithmetic-progression bound conjecture
rows.record_statement:
Let $\mathbf{t}$ denote the Thue–Morse sequence, and let $A_{\mathbf{t}}(d)$ be its associated arithmetic-progression counting function.

**Thue–Morse bound conjecture.** For all $d \geq 1$,

$$
A_{\mathbf{t}}(d) \leq d+5.
$$

Moreover, equality holds if and only if $d=2^k-1$ for some even $k \geq 2$.
The conjecture gives a sharp linear upper bound, with equality at the indicated powers-of-two-minus-one parameters.
rows.source: Bartosz Sobolewski, “On monochromatic arithmetic progressions in binary words associated with pattern sequences”, arXiv:2204.05287 (2023).
rows.what_was_proved: For every difference d >= 1, the longest monochromatic arithmetic progression of difference d in the Thue-Morse sequence has length A_t(d) <= d + 5, and A_t(d) = d + 5 exactly when d = 2^k - 1 with k even and k >= 2 (d = 3, 15, 63, 255, ...). This is Conjecture 3 of Sobolewski, for every starting point and both colours. The proof places a binomial cube S_D with D >= c - 5 inside the set of residues where the colour is forced to change, by Lucas's theorem; shows over F_2 that X^{uj}(1 + X^u)^D is divisible by (1 + X)^D, so that after multiplication by any odd u this set cannot fit in a cyclic arc shorter than D, which gives the bound; and characterizes equality by a rigidity lemma for affine cubes and three explicit families of obstructions. Lean defines the length with no cap, as the supremum over starting points of the first index at which the colour changes, in the extended naturals.

rows.title: Arithmetic conjectures for the normalized denominators of the Fabius function
rows.record_statement:
Let $D_n$ be the denominator sequence associated with the rational values of the Fabius function, and define

$$
A_n=2^{-\binom{n}{2}}D_n.
$$

For $n\geq 1$, set $K_n=A_{2n-1}$; thus $K_1=A_1$, and for $n\geq 2$,

$$
K_n=2^{-\binom{2n-1}{2}}D_{2n-1}=2^{-\binom{2n-2}{2}}D_{2n-2}.
$$

Finally, define

$$
H_n=\frac{K_n}{2(2n-1)!}.
$$

**Conjectured arithmetic properties.** The following statements appear to be true: $A_{2n}=A_{2n+1}$ for $n\geq 1$; $2(2n-1)!$ divides $K_n$; and $H_n$ is an odd integer.

These claims describe a proposed parity and divisibility pattern for the normalized denominator sequence arising in the arithmetic of the Fabius function. The supplied text presents them as observations believed to hold, but gives no proof or resolution.
rows.source: Juan Arias de Reyna, “Arithmetic of the Fabius function”, arXiv:1702.06487 (2017).
rows.what_was_proved: All three clauses of Conjecture 16 of Arias de Reyna on the common denominators of the values of the Fabius function at dyadic rationals hold: the stated coincidence of consecutive terms, the divisibility by 2(2n - 1)!, and the oddness and integrality of the normalized sequence H_n; moreover D_n is the least integer clearing all values of the function at the dyadic points of level n. Lean proves that a function satisfying the Fabius functional equation exists and is unique, derives its dyadic values from the moment recurrence, and proves the three clauses. The new mathematics is a triangular convolution with the Thue-Morse sequence, a propagation step through integer-valued polynomials, and a p-adic lemma on the first weighted minimum of a sequence of valuations.
